# Preface {.unnumbered}

Who this book is for, what it assumes, and how it relates to *Data Science in Production* (2020). The book is a spiritual successor, focused on one domain: training and serving ML models for a mobile DSP doing user acquisition.

<!-- Outline: data scientists and MLEs joining an ad tech startup, and ad tech engineers moving into ML -->

## Recommended reading (my picks)

- *Designing Machine Learning Systems* (Chip Huyen, 2022)
- *AI Engineering: Building Applications with Foundation Models* (Chip Huyen, 2025)
- *Data Science in Production* (Ben Weber, 2020)
- *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* (Martin Kleppmann)

## Related work

- Computational advertising
  - *Display Advertising with Real-Time Bidding (RTB) and Behavioural Targeting* (Wang, Zhang, and Yuan, 2017), open access
  - *Computational Advertising: Market and Technologies for Internet Commercial Monetization* (Liu and Wang, 2nd ed., 2020)
  - *Computational Advertising: Techniques for Targeting Relevant Ads* (Dave and Varma, 2014)
  - *A Practical Guide to Budget Pacing Algorithms in Digital Advertising* (arXiv, 2025)
- Programmatic advertising primers
  - *Introduction to Programmatic Advertising* (Kosorin, 2nd ed., 2022)
  - *The AdTech Book* (Clearcode), free online
- Recommender systems
  - *Deep Learning Recommender Systems* (Wang, Pu, and Wang, 2025)
  - *Building Recommendation Systems in Python and JAX* (Bischof and Yee, 2023)
- ML in production and operations
  - *Machine Learning Design Patterns* (Lakshmanan, Robinson, and Munn, 2020)
  - *Reliable Machine Learning* (Chen, Murphy, Parisa, Sculley, and Underwood, 2022)
  - *Site Reliability Engineering* (Beyer, Jones, Petoff, and Murphy, 2016), free online
- Experimentation
  - *Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments* (Kohavi, Tang, and Xu, 2020)
- Go
  - *Learning Go* (Jon Bodner, 2nd ed., 2024)
